messages.content: 你能估計2020年印度孟加拉虎的人口數量嗎？並將其與同年肯亞非洲象的估計人口數量進行比較，然後估計這兩種物種在各自國家的當前年份的人口數量嗎？

function.name: estimate_population
function.description: Estimate the population of a particular species in a given country. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

species.description: The species for which population needs to be estimated.

country.description: The country where the species lives.

year.description: The year for which population estimate is sought. Default is the current year.

message.reasoning: The user wants estimates for 2020 populations for Bengal tiger in India and African elephant in Kenya, then compare them, and estimate current year populations. We have a tool estimate_population that can estimate population for a species in a country for a given year. We need to call it twice: once for Bengal tiger in India for 2020, once for African elephant in Kenya for 2020. Then we need to compare the numbers. Then estimate current year populations: Bengal tiger in India for current year (default year), African elephant in Kenya for current year. So we need to call the tool twice more: Bengal tiger in India default year, African elephant in Kenya default year. The user didn't specify a year for current year, so we can use default. We should ask for clarification? The user asked for current year estimates, but didn't specify a year. We can assume current year is 2026. But the tool default is current year. So we can call with no year. So we need to call estimate_population twice for 2020, then compare, then estimate current year populations. We can do all four calls. The user wants the comparison and estimates. We can do the calls.
